samples.summary: New CLI + older backend = `wafflebase login` can never complete (version skew across independently released packages)
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:206 now rejects any callback whose `state` does not equal the freshly minted nonce. The echo is produced only by the backend change in packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:127-134, and the CLI ships independently to npm (.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml:52 publishes @wafflebase/cli on its own version). Any self-hosted or not-yet-upgraded backend (packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md) redirects to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=…` with no `state`, so the browser gets a bare `400 Invalid state`, the listener never resolves, and login fails after the 30s timeout at packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:257-265 with the misleading message "Login timed out". The backend side is deliberately backward compatible (nonce optional), but the CLI side is not forward/backward compatible in the other direction, and nothing detects or reports the skew. Fix belongs on the new CLI code: detect a state-less callback and emit a specific "server does not support this CLI version" error rather than hanging.

samples.summary: Silently dropping an over-long/non-string nonce makes the CLI hang instead of failing fast
samples.evidence: packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts:33-39 stores `undefined` when the nonce is empty, non-string (Express yields an array for a repeated `?nonce=`), or >128 chars. The controller then omits `&state=` (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:127-131) and the CLI's gate at packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:206 rejects the genuine callback, so a login that the backend considered fine ends in the 30s timeout with no diagnostic. Today's CLI nonce is 43 chars so this is not reachable from the shipped client, but any consumer of the documented `?nonce=` contract (docs/design/rest-api.md:334-338) that exceeds the cap gets a silent hang rather than a 400.

samples.summary: §8.1 of the CLI design doc still shows the pretty-printed multi-line envelope that §9 now forbids
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:782-790 prints the error envelope as a four-line ```json block, while the same document at docs/design/cli.md:1029-1030 (updated by this change) states the envelope is "a single JSON line on stderr". Agents and future contributors reading §8.1 will implement/expect the old shape. The top-level docs check only validates backticked paths, so nothing catches this.

samples.summary: Agent-facing skill files still document the envelope without the new `command` field
samples.evidence: packages/cli/skills/docs-read-content.md:86 and packages/cli/skills/docs-import-docx.md:57 show `{ "error": { "code": …, "message": … } }` with no `command` key, and with the old spacing. These files are the contract agents read (packages/cli/skills/SKILL.md:69 tells the agent to parse the JSON error response), so they now describe a shape the CLI no longer emits.

samples.summary: `ctx` still emits bare-text failures, contradicting the newly documented "every emitter builds it through errorEnvelope" rule
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:61 (`console.error('Not logged in. Run `wafflebase login`.')`) and :67 (`Workspace not found: …`) print unstructured text with no envelope, no code and no `command`, while docs/design/cli.md:1035-1039 — rewritten by this change — asserts that every emitter goes through `errorEnvelope`/`backendErrorEnvelope`. A line-delimited stderr reader built against the new promise will fail on these two paths. packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:73/90/107 are in the same position.

finding.summary: New CLI + older backend = `wafflebase login` can never complete (version skew across independently released packages)
finding.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:206 now rejects any callback whose `state` does not equal the freshly minted nonce. The echo is produced only by the backend change in packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:127-134, and the CLI ships independently to npm (.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml:52 publishes @wafflebase/cli on its own version). verdict.reason: All cited code checks out. login.ts:196-210 rejects any /callback lacking a matching `state` with a bare 400 and does NOT settle the promise, so the only remaining exit is the 30s timer at login.ts:257-265 which rejects with the generic "Login timed out" message. The `&state=` echo is produced solely by auth.controller.ts:126-135, added in this change and gated on the optional `state.nonce` (cli-auth.store.ts:13,48-60; github-auth.guard.ts:26-37) — i.e. the backend is explicitly backward compatible toward old CLIs, while the CLI has no tolerance, probe, or distinct error for a backend that predates the echo. npm-publish.yml:52-59 confirms @wafflebase/cli is released independently on its own version, and packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md documents source-based self-hosting (lines 20-21), so a fresh CLI against a stale backend is a real configuration. I grepped the whole repo for `nonce` and found no version negotiation or state-less fallback anywhere, and packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts only covers matching/mismatched nonce. No guard makes this unreachable and it is a cross-package contract change (new required response field) with unhandled consumers — inside the blast-radius lane.

mergedFrom.summary: Backend-shaped error bodies are printed directly with pretty-printed JSON and no `command`, bypassing the new single-line `outputError` contract

finding.summary: Out-of-diff error emitters still print multi-line pretty JSON, breaking the one-line stderr envelope contract this change now asserts and documents
finding.evidence: The change makes `outputError` emit a single line and the new test asserts `expect(raw).not.toContain('\n')` (packages/cli/test/output.test.ts:151), while README/design now state "a single JSON line on stderr" (packages/cli/README.md:116, docs/design/cli.md:1017). But many reachable error paths never go through `outputError` and still emit `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)`: packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:195 and :255, packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:154 and :204, packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts:148 and :203, packages/cli/src/commands/schema.ts:33, packages/cli/src/files/upload.ts:185/:217/:227, packages/cli/src/files/download.ts:57, packages/cli/src/slides/import.ts:152/:194/:237/:254/:311, packages/cli/src/notes/import.ts:120/:159/:188. A caller that adopts a line-delimited stderr parser because the contract now promises one line per error will fail on `docs content` / `slides import` / `files upload` failures. (The task note at docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md:19-22 scopes these to #654/#655, so this may be a knowingly-accepted gap, but the docs/tests now state the contract unconditionally.)

verdict.reason: The claimed bypassing sites do not emit pretty-printed multi-line error JSON. Every named error path routes through the shared single-line helpers `errorEnvelope`/`backendErrorEnvelope` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:75-83, :94-114), which call `JSON.stringify` with no indent: docs.ts:202-208 and :268-274, slides.ts:161-164 and :218-221, notes.ts:155-158 and :216-219, schema.ts:40-47, files/upload.ts:147-153/:164-166/:172-178/:216-222/:228-234, files/download.ts:63-69, slides/import.ts:159-165/:197-203/:246-252/:257-259/:265-271/:328, notes/import.ts:133-139/:167-173/:200-206/:211-213/:219-225. A repo-wide grep for `JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)` in packages/cli/src returns only stdout success/dry-run bodies (notes/import.ts:176,229; docs/import.ts:187,247; files/upload.ts:238; slides/import.ts:182,207,229,276; upload.ts:184), the `--format json` stdout formatter (output/json.ts:2), content renderers (notes/content.ts:77, slides/content.ts:94), dry-run stdout (client/dry-run.ts:24), and the on-disk session file (config/session.ts:68) — none is a stderr error envelope. The task note at docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md:19-22 describes the pre-change state and is stale; the code it refers to now uses the shared helpers. Ground: not-present.

finding.summary: `schema <unknown>` emits a multi-line NOT_FOUND envelope without `command`, contradicting the newly documented one-line contract
finding.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/schema.ts:32-39 writes `JSON.stringify({error:{code:'NOT_FOUND',...}}, null, 2)` and sets exitCode 1 without calling `outputError`. After this change the documented envelope is one line plus `command` (docs/design/cli.md:1017), so this reachable path (`wafflebase schema bogus`) violates it. Ironically the docstring on the new `commandPath` claims the dotted name is "the same string the `schema` command indexes on", yet schema's own error is un-attributed.

verdict.reason: The finding describes code that does not exist. It claims packages/cli/src/commands/schema.ts:32-39 hand-rolls a pretty-printed `JSON.stringify({error:{...}}, null, 2)` with no `command` field. The actual file (schema.ts:36-49) calls `errorEnvelope('NOT_FOUND', `Unknown command: ${commandName}`, commandPath(this))`, importing both helpers at schema.ts:3-8. `errorEnvelope` (formatter.ts:75-83) emits a single-line `JSON.stringify` with no indent argument and spreads in `{ command }` when supplied; `commandPath` (formatter.ts:58-64) resolves to "schema" for this command. The one-line, attributed contract is therefore satisfied, not violated. An existing end-to-end test (test/output.test.ts:538-549) runs `wafflebase schema bogus.thing` and asserts the emitted envelope is exactly `{code:'NOT_FOUND', message:'Unknown command: bogus.thing', command:'schema'}` with exitCode 1. The design doc the finding cites explicitly names this path as covered (docs/design/cli.md:1035-1039: "...and `schema`'s lookup miss"). The secondary claim that "schema's own error is un-attributed" is contradicted by schema.ts:44. Not calling `outputError` is real but intentional (an unknown name is a lookup miss, not an exception) and produces an identical wire shape, so it carries no blast-radius impact.
